problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039985/assets/37c80a68fc1ee7dd534c795a7cfae13e44f63b09df4f2e948b29acbd1fb7ff06.png)

Consider the graph of $y=f(x)$ above. Which of the following statements is true?
worked_solution:
From the graph, we see that

- The slope of the tangent at $x=-4$ is positive, so ${f}^{′}(-4)>0.$

- The slope of the tangent at $x=-3$ is zero, so ${f}^{′}(-3)=0.$

- The slope of the tangent at $x=-1$ is negative, so ${f}^{′}(-1)<0.$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(-1)<{f}^{′}(-3)<{f}^{′}(-4).$

Question 2
?

Consider the graph of y=f(x) above. Which of the following statements is true?

a
f′(−4)<f′(−1)<f′(−3)
b
f′(−3)<f′(−1)<f′(−4)
c
f′(−1)<f′(−3)<f′(−4)
d
f′(−4)<f′(−3)<f′(−1)
e
f′(−3)<f′(−4)<f′(−1)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the graph, we see that

  • The slope of the tangent at x=−4 is positive, so f′(−4)>0.

  • The slope of the tangent at x=−3 is zero, so f′(−3)=0.

  • The slope of the tangent at x=−1 is negative, so f′(−1)<0.

Therefore, f′(−1)<f′(−3)<f′(−4).
